site.activity.music.h1: Play your MIDI files on Heartopia's instruments
site.activity.music.lead: Import a song, pick the instrument you're holding in the game, and press <kbd>F6</kbd>: DodoTopia presses the keys for you, note by note, right on the file's tempo.
site.activity.music.shot_alt: DodoTopia's Music activity: song library, player, instrument picker, and the “Play in Heartopia” button.
site.activity.music.what_body:
DodoTopia reads a MIDI file and turns it into key presses for the instrument you picked: each note becomes the key that plays it in Heartopia, sent at just the right moment. It knows 19 instrument types from the game and their key layouts (15, 22, or 37 notes), and it checks the song against the instrument first: out-of-range notes, missing sharps and flats, percussion tracks. Any possible adjustments (transposing, shifting octaves, skipping notes) are offered to you along with their actual effect, never applied behind your back.

You can preview the song on your computer without launching the game, change the speed mid-playback, mute a track, and keep a song library with favorites. An optional Discord account unlocks the shared “Discover songs” library and rooms to play with friends.
site.activity.music.need.1: A MIDI file (.mid or .midi): your own files, or ones from the shared library.
site.activity.music.need.2: Heartopia open in the foreground, with the instrument equipped and its keyboard showing.
site.activity.music.need.3: The same instrument and layout selected in DodoTopia as in the game.
site.activity.music.need.4: For a few rare instruments, a one-time key setup, guided by the app.
site.activity.music.step.1.title: Import a song
site.activity.music.step.1.text: Drag a .mid file into “My library,” or grab one from “Discover songs.” DodoTopia shows you its length, its tracks, and what will be adjusted to fit the instrument.
site.activity.music.step.2.title: Pick the instrument
site.activity.music.step.2.text: In Heartopia, open your instrument. In DodoTopia, pick the same type and the same key layout.
site.activity.music.step.3.title: Start it in the game
site.activity.music.step.3.text: Press <kbd>F6</kbd> (or the “Play in Heartopia” button) and the game receives the keys. <kbd>F7</kbd>, any key, or a left click stops playback.
site.activity.music.step_note: You can preview the song on your computer before playing it in the game: nothing is sent to Heartopia.
site.activity.music.faq.1.q: The song sounds off or notes are missing. Why?
site.activity.music.faq.1.a: Most often, the instrument selected in DodoTopia isn't the one open in the game, or the key layout is different (the two 15-note layouts don't use the same keys). Also check what DodoTopia tells you before playback: a song with sharps on a diatonic instrument will lose or shift those notes, and it lets you know.
site.activity.music.faq.2.a: Nineteen types, from the piano to the conch shell, listed on the Instruments page along with the real status of their key profiles. Six of them still need their keys mapped: you set those up by hand in the app before you can play them.
site.activity.music.faq.3.q: Can I preview a song without opening the game?
site.activity.music.faq.3.a: Yes: “Preview on this computer” plays the song with a synthesized sound, without sending anything to any window. It's the best way to check a file or a transposition before starting it in Heartopia.
site.activity.music.faq.4.q: Where can I find MIDI files?
site.activity.music.faq.4.a: In DodoTopia's shared library (“Discover songs,” with a Discord account), uploaded and moderated by the community, or anywhere else: DodoTopia reads any standard MIDI file. Only share files you have the rights to.
site.activity.draw.h1: Recreate any image on a Heartopia canvas, square by square
site.activity.draw.lead: Pick a photo or a drawing: DodoTopia converts it to the game's colors, shows you exactly how it will look, then paints it for you with the pencil and the paint bucket.
site.activity.draw.shot_alt: DodoTopia's Drawing activity: preview of the image converted to the game's palette, canvas size, and color settings.
site.activity.draw.what_body:
DodoTopia scales your image down to the canvas size you chose in the game and converts it to Heartopia's palette (16 swatches and their shades). The preview shows exactly what will be painted, with a square count for each color. Once started, it paints one color at a time: the paint bucket for large areas, the pencil for everything else, then it rereads the screen to go back over any squares it missed.

An interrupted drawing picks up right where it left off: start it again on the same canvas and only the missing squares get painted. While it's drawing, don't touch the mouse or keyboard: the slightest movement stops everything and hands control back to you.
site.activity.draw.need.2: A blank canvas open in Heartopia, at the chosen size, with detail set to maximum and the grid turned on.
site.activity.draw.need.3: A game area setup, done once per resolution: thirteen spots to hover over, with step-by-step guidance.
site.activity.draw.need.4: Some time to spare: a large canvas means thousands of clicks.
site.activity.draw.step.1.title: Import the image
site.activity.draw.step.1.text: DodoTopia shows you the square-by-square result and the selected size. Adjust the framing, colors, and dithering until you like the preview.
site.activity.draw.step.2.title: Get the canvas ready
site.activity.draw.step.2.text: In Heartopia, open a blank canvas at that size. The first time, follow “Set up the game area” to show where the canvas, palette, and tools are.
site.activity.draw.step.3.title: Start it and hands off
site.activity.draw.step.3.text: Press <kbd>F6</kbd>. DodoTopia paints, rereads the screen, and fixes mistakes. Any key or mouse movement stops the drawing; it will pick up later where it left off.
site.activity.draw.step_note: The result depends on the game's palette: a photo with lots of subtle shading turns into a drawing with flat colors. The preview is accurate, so check it before you start.
site.activity.draw.faq.1.q: The drawing is off by one square. What should I do?
site.activity.draw.faq.1.a: Redo the game area setup for that canvas size, using the same resolution and window layout. DodoTopia also measures the actual grid origin live from the first color onward, but an accurate calibration is still the foundation.
site.activity.draw.faq.2.q: How long does a drawing take?
site.activity.draw.faq.2.a: Anywhere from a few minutes for a small canvas to well over an hour for a large, detailed one: every square is a click, and the game sets the pace. The screen shows your progress and the estimated time.
site.activity.draw.faq.3.q: Can I use my computer in the meantime?
site.activity.draw.faq.3.a: No: DodoTopia controls your mouse and keyboard, and the game has to stay in the foreground. Any movement on your end stops the drawing — that's on purpose, so you get control back instantly.
site.activity.draw.faq.4.a: The game's canvas sizes (for example 140 × 84 or 150 × 150 squares): “Auto” picks the one that best fits the image, or you can choose one yourself. The canvas must be open at the same size in Heartopia.
site.activity.cook.h1: Cook the same recipe over and over in Heartopia
site.activity.cook.lead: Cook it once yourself, stand in front of the stove, and hit start: DodoTopia restarts the recipe, clicks the spatula at the right moment, and collects the dish, as many times as you like.
site.activity.cook.shot_alt: DodoTopia's Cooking activity: number of dishes, tracked stoves, and loop status.
site.activity.cook.what_body:
DodoTopia watches the bubble above the stove and recognizes its icons: it restarts the last recipe you cooked, waits for the green ring, clicks the spatula, collects the dish, and starts again. It can keep an eye on several stoves at once and stops on its own once it reaches the number of dishes you asked for, or when you run out of ingredients.

It doesn't pick the recipe: it repeats whichever one the game offers last. Any mouse movement or key press stops the loop immediately.
site.activity.cook.need.1: The recipe's ingredients, enough for the number of dishes you want.
site.activity.cook.need.2: Your character in front of the stove, with the bubble visible and the game in the foreground.
site.activity.cook.need.3: A kitchen setup, done once: the bubble's position and a capture of its icons.
site.activity.cook.step.1.title: Cook it once yourself
site.activity.cook.step.1.text: Make the recipe you want in the game: DodoTopia repeats the stove's last recipe; it doesn't choose one.
site.activity.cook.step.2.title: Set up the kitchen
site.activity.cook.step.2.text: In front of the stove, with the bubble visible, follow “Set up the kitchen”: the assistant records the bubble's position and captures its icons. A detection test tells you whether everything is recognized.
site.activity.cook.step.3.title: Choose how many dishes and start
site.activity.cook.step.3.text: Pick an exact number or “nonstop,” then press <kbd>F6</kbd>. DodoTopia clicks at the right moment, collects, and starts again. <kbd>F7</kbd>, any key, or the mouse stops the loop.
site.activity.cook.step_note: Leaving the kitchen running for hours is heavy use of an unofficial tool: that's your choice and your responsibility.
site.activity.cook.faq.1.a: Run the detection test in front of the stove, then recapture its icons if the game's look has changed or your resolution has. The bubble must be fully visible, with no window covering it.
site.activity.cook.faq.2.q: How many stoves can it keep track of?
site.activity.cook.faq.2.a: Several, each with its own configured bubble position. DodoTopia checks them in turn and clicks whichever one shows the green ring. The number of dishes you ask for covers all of them combined.
site.activity.cook.faq.3.q: What happens when I run out of ingredients?
site.activity.cook.faq.3.a: The recipe won't restart; DodoTopia notices after a few tries and stops cleanly, telling you why, instead of clicking away at nothing.
site.activity.together.h1: Play the same song at the same moment, each on your own instrument
site.activity.together.lead: Two ways to start in sync: an online room with a six-character code, or sound-based sync with no network needed. Everyone keeps their own instrument and part.
site.activity.together.shot_alt: DodoTopia's “Play together” view: online room with its code, players present, and the button to start the session.
site.activity.together.what_body:
In an online room, one player creates the room and shares its code; the others join, everyone picks their instrument, and the leader chooses the song and starts the session: DodoTopia lines up everyone's start with the server clock. The song is shared only for the length of the session, and nothing is saved.

Sound-based sync needs no account and no network: the first player plays a cue note in the game, the other players' DodoTopia hears it through the mic, and everyone starts at the same moment. Starts are lined up as closely as possible, not perfectly: results depend on your computer and your connection.
site.activity.together.need.1: Every player with DodoTopia and the same MIDI file (the room shares it automatically).
site.activity.together.need.2: For an online room: a Discord account and an internet connection; for sound-based sync: a mic and a bit of quiet.
site.activity.together.need.3: Everyone with their instrument open in Heartopia, in the same place in the game.
site.activity.together.step.1.title: Create or join a room
site.activity.together.step.1.text: From Music › Play together: the leader creates the room and shares its six-character code; the others enter it.
site.activity.together.step.2.title: Everyone picks an instrument
site.activity.together.step.2.text: The leader chooses the song, and each player picks the instrument they're holding in the game. Everyone can see who's ready.
site.activity.together.step.3.title: Start the session
site.activity.together.step.3.text: The leader hits start: DodoTopia runs a shared countdown and starts playback for everyone at the same moment. A key press stops your playback, not anyone else's.
site.activity.together.step_note: No account or network? Choose “Sound-based sync”: a cue note played by the first player acts as the starting signal.
site.activity.together.faq.1.q: Do I need an account to play together?
site.activity.together.faq.1.a: For online rooms, yes: a Discord login, used only to identify you (username and avatar). Sound-based sync works with no account at all.
site.activity.together.faq.2.a: No. Starts are lined up on a shared clock to within a few tens of milliseconds, but lag from the game and your computer adds up on top. It sounds great, just not like a studio recording.
site.activity.together.faq.3.a: Up to eight. A player who disconnects keeps their spot for a minute; an empty room closes on its own.
site.download.lead: Free, no account required, for Windows 10 and 11 and for Linux. Every file is published with its SHA-256 checksum, and after that, the app keeps itself up to date.
site.download.soon_text: No version has been released yet. The first downloadable version is on its way: check back in a few days, and this page will offer the Windows installer, the portable version and the Linux archive.
site.download.windows.title: Windows — installer
site.download.windows.desc: The recommended option: DodoTopia in your Start menu, automatic updates, and a clean uninstall.
site.download.windows.missing: This release doesn't include a Windows installer.
site.download.portable.title: Windows — portable version
site.download.portable.desc: An archive you unzip wherever you like, no installation needed; you update it by hand.
site.download.portable.missing: No portable version for this release.
site.download.linux.title: Linux — archive
site.download.linux.desc: A tar.gz archive for x86-64 (X11). Extract it, then run DodoTopia.
site.download.linux.missing: This release doesn't include a Linux archive.
site.download.sha_note: The SHA-256 checksum lets you confirm that the file you received is exactly the one that was published: the app checks it automatically on every update, and VirusTotal scans it with about sixty antivirus engines.
site.download.macos_note: DodoTopia doesn't work on macOS, phones or tablets: it needs to send keystrokes and read the screen of a Windows or Linux computer running the game.
site.download.minreq.1: Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), or Linux x86-64 with X11 (Wayland isn't supported).
site.download.minreq.2: Heartopia installed and playable on the same computer, in windowed or borderless windowed mode.
site.download.minreq.3: About 300 MB of disk space and 2 GB of free memory on top of the game.
site.download.minreq.4: For online rooms: an internet connection and a Discord account (optional).
site.download.installed_text: When it starts, DodoTopia asks this server whether a newer version exists (sending only its version and platform, nothing else), checks the manifest signature and the file's checksum, then offers to install it. No need to come back here.
site.download.portable_text: The installer puts DodoTopia in your Start menu and updates itself: that's the recommended option. The portable version unzips wherever you like, without admin rights, but you'll have to replace it by hand with each new version.
site.download.smartscreen_text: That's expected for a lesser-known app that sends keystrokes and reads the screen: Windows doesn't recognize the publisher yet. The file is exactly the one published here (see the SHA-256 checksum above), and you can have it scanned on VirusTotal before opening it.
site.download.smartscreen_steps: To continue, click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. Never do this for a file downloaded from anywhere other than this site.
site.news.lead: What changes in each release. Updates install automatically from the app; this page keeps a record of the last twenty published releases.
site.news.empty_text: No release has been published yet. Notes for the first release will show up here.
site.community.lead: DodoTopia is made by players, for players. The song library, the instrument key maps and the bug reports all come from the community.
site.community.discord_text: Questions, help, songs, release announcements and key mappings for the instruments that still need them: it all happens there.
site.community.discord_missing: The community server isn't open yet. In the meantime, write to {email} with any question or suggestion.
site.community.contribute_intro: The app's “Discover songs” library is fed by players and moderated before anything goes live. Here's how to submit a file.
site.community.contribute.1.title: Sign in with Discord
site.community.contribute.1.text: From the avatar at the top of the app. Only your username and avatar are read; DodoTopia never sees your email address or your messages.
site.community.contribute.2.title: Upload the file
site.community.contribute.2.text: In “Discover songs” › Suggest a song: a title, an artist, and the .mid file (2 MB max, at least 10 notes, 30 minutes at most).
site.community.contribute.3.title: Wait for moderation
site.community.contribute.3.text: A moderator checks that the file plays correctly and that nothing is off. Once approved, it shows up for everyone, and you can remove it at any time.
site.community.contribute_note: Only upload files you have the rights to: your own compositions, public-domain works, or files whose license allows sharing.
site.community.rule.1: Respect other players: no insults, harassment or hateful content, here or in the game.
site.community.rule.2: No misleading or promotional titles, usernames or artists, and no impersonating anyone.
site.community.rule.3: No malformed files, and no attempts to overload or get around the service.
site.community.rule.4: What you share must be yours or freely shareable.
site.community.rule.5: Serious or repeated violations lead to content removal and account closure.
site.community.report_text: The easiest way is the report button next to each song in the app. For a copyright takedown request, write to {email} with the song, the reason, and proof of your rights.
site.community.help_text: FAQs and troubleshooting are on the page
site.help.lead: Answers to the questions we hear most, followed by the usual problems and how to fix them. If nothing matches, write to us: we do reply.
site.help.trouble_lead: Listed in the order they usually come up: when downloading, on first launch, then during an activity.
site.help.contact_text: To report a problem, email {email} and tell us what you were doing, what happened, and which version of the app you have (Settings › About).
site.help.logs_text: Please attach your logs: they live in the %APPDATA%\DodoTopia folder (dodotopia.log, dessin.log, cuisine.log, multi.log), and you can open it from Settings › About and updates.
site.help.faq.1.a: Yes, completely. DodoTopia is free, with no ads, no in-app purchases, no subscription and no hidden paid version. You only need a Discord account if you want to share your songs or play in a room; everything else — music, drawing, cooking — works without an account and offline.
site.help.faq.2.a: On a Windows 10 or 11 computer, and on Linux (X11) whenever an archive is published for the current version. There's no macOS version, and nothing for phones or tablets: DodoTopia has to send keystrokes and read the screen of the machine the game is running on.
site.help.faq.3.q: Does the game need to be open?
site.help.faq.3.a: Yes. DodoTopia doesn't play on its own in a vacuum: it presses keys and clicks inside the Heartopia window, which has to be open and in the foreground. Before sending anything, it checks that the game is the active window, and stops if it isn't. You can, however, preview a song without launching the game: in that case, nothing is sent anywhere.
site.help.faq.4.q: Could my game account get in trouble?
site.help.faq.4.a:
To be honest: it's possible, and we can't guarantee anything. DodoTopia is an unofficial tool with no connection whatsoever to Heartopia's publishers. The game's terms of service prohibit bots and unauthorized software, and the publisher is free to take action against any account as it sees fit.

DodoTopia doesn't inject anything into the game, doesn't modify any game files and doesn't read its memory: it simply presses keys and looks at the screen, the way a very fast person would. That lowers the risk, but doesn't remove it. You use it at your own risk.
site.help.faq.5.a: For music, MIDI files: .mid and .midi. For drawing, .png, .jpg, .gif, .bmp and .webp images. Imported files are copied into your DodoTopia folder; the original is left untouched.
site.help.faq.6.q: Is there any setup to do first?
site.help.faq.6.a: For music, no: pick the instrument and start (a few instruments ask you to check or record their keys once). For drawing and cooking, yes, once: DodoTopia needs to know where the canvas, the palette, the tools or the stove's bubble are on your screen. A wizard walks you through it one position at a time, and the setup is saved. You'll need to redo it if you change your resolution or window layout.
site.help.faq.7.q: How do I stop an automation that's running?
site.help.faq.7.a: F7 stops everything by default, and you can change the shortcut. While drawing or cooking, any key press or mouse movement also works; while playing in the game, a key press or a left click stops playback. The screen always shows the actual current state and the stop button.
site.help.faq.8.a:
No. But let's be upfront about what the app does, because it's unusual: DodoTopia sends key presses and mouse clicks to the game window, and reads the image on your screen. That's exactly what you ask it to do. Those two behaviors are also what a keylogger does, which is why Windows SmartScreen or an antivirus may show a warning the first time you run it.

What DodoTopia does not do: record what you type anywhere, snoop through your other windows, touch your passwords, or send your screenshots anywhere — they're analyzed in memory on your machine and then discarded. Without an account, the only thing sent over the network is the update check. The details are in the privacy policy.
site.help.faq.9.a: Offline, none: your MIDI files, images, settings and logs stay on your computer. The app contacts this server only to check whether an update is available (installed version and platform), and, if you sign in with Discord, for the shared library and rooms. In that case the server stores your Discord ID, your username, your avatar URL, your sessions and the files you upload.
site.help.faq.10.q: How do I play with others?
site.help.faq.10.a: Go to Music › Play together: either an online room (six-character code, Discord account) where the leader gives the start signal, or sound-based sync, with no network, where a cue note acts as the starting signal. It's all explained on the Play together page.
site.help.trouble.1.a: That's expected for a little-known app that sends keystrokes and reads the screen. Make sure you downloaded the file from this site, optionally compare its SHA-256 hash with the one on the Download page or scan it on VirusTotal, then click “More info” › “Run anyway”.
site.help.trouble.2.q: The game doesn't receive keystrokes (nothing happens, or “injection refused”)
site.help.trouble.2.a: There are two usual causes. If Heartopia was launched as administrator, Windows won't let a regular app send it keystrokes: restart DodoTopia as administrator (right-click › Run as administrator), or restart the game without elevation. Also, the game has to be in the foreground when you start: DodoTopia checks this and tells you. “Test a note” in Settings confirms that keystrokes are getting through.
site.help.trouble.3.q: Playback stops on its own: “the game is no longer in the foreground”
site.help.trouble.3.a: That's a safeguard: if another window comes to the front (a notification, Discord, your browser), the keystrokes would end up in that app. DodoTopia stops as soon as Heartopia is no longer the active window. Bring the game back to the front and start again; you can set the name of the watched program in Settings › Game program (leave it empty to skip the check).
site.help.trouble.4.q: AZERTY keyboard: the notes don't match
site.help.trouble.4.a: DodoTopia sends key positions, not letters: the game gets the right key whether your keyboard is AZERTY (French) or QWERTY. Only the labels shown on screen change, in Settings › Keyboard. If the notes are still wrong, the instrument or layout selected in DodoTopia doesn't match the one in the game.
site.help.trouble.5.q: The drawing is offset or some cells are missing
site.help.trouble.5.a: Run “Set up the game area” again for that canvas format, at the same resolution. Make sure detail level is set to maximum and the grid is turned on in the game. To resume an interrupted drawing, just start it again on the same canvas: only the missing cells get painted.
site.help.trouble.6.a: Stand in front of the stove with its bubble fully visible, and run the detection test from the Cooking activity. If it fails, capture the bubble's icons again: they change with the resolution, and sometimes with a game update.
site.help.trouble.7.a: DodoTopia checks the manifest's signature and the downloaded file's hash: if either one doesn't match, it refuses to install, just to be safe. Try again later, or download the latest version from the Download page and install it over your current one: your settings are kept.
site.instruments.lead: The {total} types of Heartopia instruments available in DodoTopia, sorted by family. Pick the same instrument in DodoTopia and in the game, then start your song.

site.instruments.state.documented.label: Documented profile, needs verifying
site.instruments.state.documented.text: A key map published by a community project exists for this type. It hasn't been tested in the game from this site: DodoTopia offers it, and it gets verified on your computer.
site.instruments.state.candidate.label: Candidate mapping, test required
site.instruments.state.candidate.text: Community maps assign notes to this percussion instrument, but nothing proves that each hit produces that pitch. DodoTopia asks for a percussion-specific test before letting it play a song.
site.instruments.state.unknown.label: Keys to be mapped
site.instruments.state.unknown.text: No documented key map for this type yet. The instrument is in DodoTopia and its keys can be set up by hand, but it can't play a song until that's done.
site.instruments.summary_unknown: Note count and range to be mapped
site.instruments.one_card_note: One card per type: the color and style variants in the game's catalog share the same sound and the same keys, so they're grouped together and don't appear separately. Instrument names are suggested translations, not the game's official labels; English names still work in the app's search.
site.instruments.layouts_text: An instrument type can support several layouts: they're settings on its profile, not different instruments. In DodoTopia, pick the same layout shown in the game.
site.instruments.layouts_note: Heads up: the two 15-note layouts don't just look different, they use different physical keys. And the number of rows won't tell you the number of notes. Octave convention: {convention}, written C4 in this page's labels.
site.instruments.sources_text: Catalog compiled on {date}. It isn't an official list and may not be complete: a type confirmed by a reliable source can be added, with its own status. The key maps come from public community projects, credited below; they describe what those projects published, nothing more.
site.instruments.provenance_text: The icons on this page are served from this server, using the files bundled with DodoTopia: no image is loaded from a third-party site. They come from Heartopia's public item catalog as listed by Build Heartopia. Being publicly available doesn't make them free to reuse: if a rights holder wants an image taken down, just write to {email} — the image will be removed and replaced with a generic badge, without the instrument leaving the list or its keys changing.
site.instruments.variants_n: {n} cosmetic variants grouped into a single type
site.instruments.teaser_lead: DodoTopia knows {total} Heartopia instrument types: one card per type, never one per color. You pick the one you've opened in the game, and DodoTopia uses its own key map — not the piano's.

site.privacy.intro: This page sets out exactly which personal data the DodoTopia service (the {host} website and its associated server) processes, why it is processed, how long it is kept, and how you can exercise your rights. It describes how the service actually works, database field by database field.
site.privacy.audience_off: not enabled on this site at the moment
site.privacy.s1.title: 1. Controller
site.privacy.s2.title: 2. The essentials in three sentences
site.privacy.s2.body:
• The application installed on your computer works offline: your MIDI files, images, settings, calibrations and logs never leave your machine.
  • The server only processes personal data if you sign in with Discord, for the shared library, the drawing gallery, import by link and online rooms. A drawing or a song only leaves your machine if you choose to publish it.
  • No data is sold, rented, transferred to a third party, or used for advertising or profiling. There are no cookies, and audience measurement, if enabled, works without cookies or identifiers (section 5).
site.privacy.s3.title: 3. Data processed, purpose and legal basis
site.privacy.s3.body:
DataWhyLegal basisRetention period
Discord ID (account number), display name and avatar image address (a URL pointing to Discord's servers)To identify you consistently, show who uploaded a song and who is present in a room, and enforce administration rights and bansPerformance of the service you requested (contract)For as long as the account exists; deleted on request or from within the application

site.privacy.s4.title: 4. Online rooms: nothing is stored
site.privacy.s4.body: Synchronized rooms exist only in the server's memory. The room code, the display name, the chosen instrument, the game state and the temporary song shared for the session are not written to any database: they disappear when the room empties or when the server restarts. The file shared in a room is stored in a temporary folder and automatically deleted a few hours after it was uploaded.
site.privacy.s5.title: 5. Website audience measurement
site.privacy.s5.body: The website may use audience measurement without cookies, without identifiers and without cross-site tracking (current status: {audience_status}). When it is active, a small script counts page views, country and device type in aggregate form: no IP address is kept, no individual profile is built, and it is not possible to identify a person from these figures. The script is not loaded if your browser sends the Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control signal: that is your opt-out, with no banner and no setting to hunt for. These figures are used solely to find out which pages are read and in which language.
site.privacy.s6.title: 6. Checking that the game is in the foreground
site.privacy.s6.body: To avoid sending keystrokes to another application, DodoTopia checks, on your computer, which window is active at the moment it acts: it reads the program name of the foreground window and compares it with the configured name (Heartopia by default). This check is strictly local: the list of your windows, the names of open programs and the contents of your screen never leave your machine and are neither stored nor transmitted. You can disable it by clearing the “Game program” setting.
site.privacy.s7.title: 7. Download counter
site.privacy.s7.body: Each published file (installer, portable version, Linux archive) has a download counter: a simple number per file, incremented by one for each completed download, with no IP address, no individual timestamp and no other information. The totals are public (home page and /api/stats) and are used to measure the usage of each version.
site.privacy.s8.title: 8. What is not collected
site.privacy.s8.body:
• No screen content, no screenshots, no keystrokes: all of this is analysed locally by the application and never transmitted.
  • No email address: Discord sign-in uses the identify scope, which gives access to neither your email address, nor your servers, nor your messages.
  • No password: the service does not create any, and your Discord password is never seen by DodoTopia.
  • No advertising cookies, no third-party trackers, and no fonts or scripts loaded from an external service, apart from the audience measurement script described in section 5 when it is enabled: this website only loads its own files.
site.privacy.s9.title: 9. Recipients
site.privacy.s9.body:
The data is accessible only to the publisher and to designated administrator accounts, solely for moderation purposes. It is not sold, rented or transferred. The only technical third parties involved are:

  • Discord, for authentication: when you sign in, your browser communicates with Discord under its own privacy policy. Avatar images are served by Discord's servers.
  • the server's hosting provider: {hoster}, whose servers are located in France, in the Marseille data centre.
  • where applicable, the audience measurement service described in section 5, which receives neither cookies nor identifiers.
site.privacy.s10.title: 10. Security
site.privacy.s10.body: Communications with the server use HTTPS. Session tokens are never stored in plain text: only their SHA-256 fingerprint is kept, which makes the database contents useless for signing in on your behalf. Uploaded files are analysed and size-capped before being accepted. The sessions of a banned account are deleted immediately. Update manifests are signed, and every downloaded file is verified against its fingerprint.
site.privacy.s11.title: 11. Your rights
site.privacy.s11.body:
In accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the French Data Protection Act (loi « Informatique et Libertés »), you have the following rights over your data: access (obtaining a copy of the data concerning you), rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, objection on legitimate grounds, and portability of the data you have provided.

In practice:

  • you can yourself delete, at any time and from within the application, the songs you have uploaded, and delete your account;
  • signing out immediately deletes the corresponding session;
  • for any other request (a copy of your data, complete deletion), write to {email} stating your Discord username. You will receive a response within one month at the latest.

If, after contacting us, you believe that your rights have not been respected, you may lodge a complaint with the competent supervisory authority, which in France is the CNIL.
site.privacy.s12.title: 12. Children
site.privacy.s12.body: Sign-in goes through Discord, whose terms impose a minimum age. The service is not intended for children below that age and does not knowingly collect any data about them.
site.privacy.s13.title: 13. Changes
site.privacy.s13.body: This policy may change if the service changes. The date of the last update appears at the top of the page; in the event of a substantial change, notice will be given in the application. See also the Terms of Use and the Legal Notice.
